title: Monthly Roadmap Pulse: cross-functional decision lattice and escalation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: produce a compact monthly 'pulse' packet that combines roadmap signals, three concrete decision asks, and an actionable escalation playbook for the exec reading group. This ticket coordinates cross-functional inputs (engineering capacity, infra cost modelling, reliability SLOs, and design readiness) and produces the deliverables for the upcoming review slot.

Scope and deliverables:
- One-pager executive packet with three prioritized asks and win/loss scenarios for each ask.
- Decision lattice diagram mapping options -> tradeoffs -> recommended guardrails.
- Escalation playbook: triggers, owners, and fallbacks if SLOs or budget thresholds are breached during rollout.
- Appendix: short data appendices (latency/cost delta tables, canary success criteria, customer impact map).

Key context and constraints:
- We must balance latency SLO improvements (serving runtime optimizations) against projected unit-cost increases from dedicated capacity.
- Several dependent infra changes are on the schedule for runtime-1.22 which may shift throughput by +12-20%. Those changes are tracked in ENG-1973.
- Board-level ask preference: concise tradeoffs and clear revenue/ops implications, not deep technical detail.

Decision asks (draft):
1) Approve incremental Dedicated capacity top-up for EMEA region (commit: 6 months) to avoid cross-region fallbacks during expected Q3 peak. Ask: approve budget reallocation of up to $X/month and delegated sign-off owner (Infra lead).
2) Greenlight canary expansion of batching + KV-cache patch on runtime-1.22 (criteria: <5% p99 latency regression, <3% error increase). Ask: permission to proceed with canary to 10% of traffic with automatic rollback.
3) Prioritize a small scope experiment on quantization profiles tied to common prompt families (3 models). Ask: allocate 3 dedicated GPUs for 8 weeks and accept 2% potential MRR risk during evaluation.

Open trade-offs and risks:
- Cost vs. reliability: committing Dedicated capacity reduces fallback risk but increases fixed cost.
- Quality regressions from new kernels: must be guarded by prompt-set evals to prevent customer regressions.
- Timeline coupling: if ENG-4820 (kernel scheduler improvements) slips, canary window must be extended.

Data & artifacts (links):
- Confluence packet (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/roadmap/pulse-2026-03 (internal)
- Canary runbook draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/canary-runbooks/runtime-1.22
- Cost delta workbook (sensitive): https://spreadsheets.redwood.ai/d/DELTAS-2026-Q2 (view restricted)
- Relevant PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821, https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1910

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- Completed one-pager and slide deck uploaded to Confluence and shared with exec by 2026-03-18.
- Decision lattice and escalation playbook reviewed and signed-off by Eng Director and Head of SRE.
- Canary runbook attached with testing metrics and automatic rollback thresholds.

Execution plan & owners:
- PM lead: Marco Chen (owner of packet coordination).
- Eng reviewers: Priya Nair (runtime), Daniel Ortiz (SRE).
- Design: Riley Thompson (two slides visualizing the lattice).
- Finance: liaison Erin Gomez for budget confirmations.

Notes on cadence and follow-ups:
- Draft packet will be shared 72 hours before the pre-read cut-off.
- Blocker escalation path: if ENG dependencies miss code freeze by >3 business days, escalate to VP Eng and pause any board asks that increase spend.
